title: GeoReasoner: Geo-localization with Reasoning in Street Views using a Large Vision-Language Model

en.text: Show a person a random street photo and, given a few seconds, they can often name the country and sometimes the city. They do it by reading clues: the script on a shop sign, the color of a license plate, the style of a lamppost, which side of the road the cars keep to. The online communities behind games like GeoGuessr and Tuxun have turned this skill into a craft, cataloguing thousands of such tells. Machine geo-localization systems, by contrast, tend to hand back a bare coordinate and no explanation a person could follow.

That silence is the problem GeoReasoner sets out to fix. Presented at ICML 2024 by researchers from HKUST (Guangzhou), Tongji University, and collaborators, the paper argues that street-view geo-localization carries two entangled blind spots. The data problem: street-view datasets are polluted with images shot in tunnels, against blank walls, or of roadside greenery, none of which contain a usable clue. The reasoning problem: retrieval and classification models are black boxes that return a location with no explanation a human can inspect or trust. GeoReasoner treats the two as one, fixing data quality and interpretability together.

en.caption: Figure 1. Three paradigms for street-view geo-localization. Retrieval-based methods (top-left) match a query against a geo-tagged gallery; classification-based methods (bottom-left) bin the globe into cells; GeoReasoner's LVLM-based approach (right) predicts a location together with a human-readable reason, and screens training images by locatability.

en.text: Its recipe is to pair a large vision-language model (LVLM) with human inference knowledge harvested from geo-games, and to feed the model only street views that are actually locatable. The payoff is a system that beats the strongest comparable LVLM, Qwen-VL, by 25.02% at the country level and 38.61% at the city level in F1, and edges out a specialist built for geo-localization on far less data while still showing its work at every step.
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18572    Code: https://github.com/lingli1996/GeoReasoner
Two blind spots: dirty data and black-box predictions

Retrieval-based methods find the nearest neighbor in a geo-tagged gallery and return its coordinates; their accuracy is capped by how complete that gallery is, which is expensive to curate. Classification-based methods carve the map into cells and predict a cell; they ignore semantic cues such as the text on a signboard and, like retrieval, cannot say why. Both also inherit whatever noise sits in the training set, and street-view collections are noisy. A model trained on images with no findable content learns very little, so the authors start by cleaning the data itself.
Quantifying whether an image can be located at all

The authors' first move is to make locatability measurable. Intuitively, a street view is locatable when it contains something a person could reason from, a legible sign, a distinctive facade, a landmark, and unlocatable when it is a tunnel wall or a hedge that could be anywhere. The contrast is stark once you put a number on it.

en.caption: Figure 5. What locatability looks like. Top row: highly locatable street views (loc. = 0.70 to 0.71) carry signboards, distinctive architecture, and landmarks. Bottom row: low-locatability views (loc. = 0.08 to 0.19) show a tunnel, a blank wall, and generic vegetation, with no usable geographic clue.

en.text: Concretely, locatability is a weighted sum over the semantic content of an image. MaskFormer segments each street view into classes (building, sky, vehicle, vegetation, and so on) and reports the area ratio of each. Sentence-BERT then scores how relevant each class is to the textual clues mined from geo-games, producing a weight per class. The locatability of an image is the dot product of its class-area vector with these relevance weights. Images scoring above a threshold of 0.4 are kept; applying the filter shrinks a raw pool of 130,000 street views down to roughly 70,000 high-quality ones.
The relevance weights themselves come from a CLIP image-text pairing network, which learns to align pictures with words without any extra manual labels.

en.caption: Figure 2. The locatability quantization network. A CLIP pairing of street-view images against text clues mined from geo-games yields an image-text similarity matrix, which is reduced to a single locatability score per image.

en.text: Text clues from the games (for example, green signs with white lettering indicate highways in South Korea) are embedded by a text encoder; street views are embedded by an image encoder; the similarity between the two modalities gives each image a single locatability score. Beyond the game clues that already exist, the network needs no extra manual annotation to do its job.
GeoReasoner: reason first, then localize

With clean data in hand, the model is built on Qwen-VL, a vision encoder, a vision-language adapter, and a pre-trained LLM, and fine-tuned in two stages with lightweight LoRA adapters, so the base weights stay frozen throughout.

en.caption: Figure 3. GeoReasoner's architecture and two-stage fine-tuning. Built on Qwen-VL (Vision Encoder, VL Adapter, pre-trained LLM), it first learns country-level reasoning (Stage 1, LoRA 1) on game clues, then sharpens city-level prediction (Stage 2, LoRA 2) on curated street views; at inference it returns country, city, and reasons.

en.text: Stage 1, reasoning tuning, trains LoRA 1 on about 3,000 text-image clue pairs from GeoGuessr and Tuxun, teaching the model to name a country and explain the visual evidence for it. Stage 2, location tuning, stacks a second adapter, LoRA 2, and trains on the 70,000 curated street views, sharpening fine-grained city-level prediction. At inference the model answers in a fixed JSON form, country, city, and a list of reasons, so every prediction ships with its justification attached.
Results: smaller data, higher accuracy, and an explanation

On a held-out set of street views, GeoReasoner reaches a country-level F1 of 0.9033 and a city-level F1 of 0.8585. That is 25.02% above Qwen-VL at the country level and 38.61% above it at the city level. More striking, it slightly surpasses StreetCLIP, a model built specifically for geo-localization and trained on 1.1M street views, despite using only 70,000 of them.

en.caption: Table 1. Precision, Recall, and F1 for country-level and city-level geo-localization. * marks the model trained on high-locatability street views; GeoReasoner leads both F1 columns.

en.text: Where do the gains come from? An ablation on data composition isolates the effect of quality alone, holding the training budget fixed.

en.caption: Figure 7. Data quality drives accuracy. As the share of high-locatability images in training rises from 0% to 100%, both country-level (blue) and city-level (orange) accuracy climb steadily, confirming that curation, not just volume, powers the gains.

en.text: Holding everything else fixed and varying only the fraction of high-locatability images in the training mix, accuracy rises steadily at both levels as that fraction grows from 0% to 100%. Quality, not sheer volume, is doing the work here.
Numbers aside, the qualitative behavior is really the point of the paper, and it is easiest to appreciate side by side.

en.caption: Figure 8. Geo-localization with reasoning, side by side. For three street views, GeoReasoner matches or beats LLaVA, Qwen-VL, and GPT-4V, and unlike the black-box baselines it explains each prediction (correct answers in green, useful clues in blue).

en.text: On a Singapore street the ComfortDelGro taxi gives GeoReasoner the answer; on the Las Vegas Strip it reads the neon and the replica landmarks; in Lhasa it cites Tibetan script and the Chinese flag. LLaVA and Qwen-VL often miss or guess without support, and while GPT-4V reasons well, GeoReasoner matches it on a fraction of a specialist's training budget.
What the two stages each contribute

A second ablation separates the two fine-tuning stages. Starting from the Qwen-VL baseline (0.7225 / 0.5270 country/city F1), reasoning tuning alone lifts the model to 0.8215 / 0.5813, and location tuning alone to 0.8766 / 0.8255. Only with both stacked does GeoReasoner reach 0.9033 / 0.8585. Location tuning supplies most of the city-level precision, while reasoning tuning adds a further lift and, crucially, supplies the explanations that make each answer legible.

en.caption: Table 2. Ablation over the two fine-tuning stages. Reasoning tuning and location tuning are complementary; the full two-stage model wins on every F1.

en.text: Takeaway

GeoReasoner's headline lesson is that you do not need millions of street views to build a state-of-the-art geo-localizer; you need the right images and the right knowledge. Quantifying which views are locatable, and borrowing the inference tricks humans use to win geo-games, lets a two-stage LVLM match or beat specialist models on a fraction of the data while explaining every call. The honest boundary: the model still stumbles on genuine ambiguity, unable to tell the real Eiffel Tower in Paris from its replicas in Las Vegas and Hangzhou, and its knowledge reaches only as far as the clues the game communities have written down. Even so, it points a practical path toward geo-localization that is at once interpretable and efficient with training data.

zh.text: 给一个人看一张随手拍的街景照片，几秒钟内他往往能说出国家，有时还能说出城市。靠的是读线索：店招上的文字、车牌的颜色、路灯的样式、车辆靠哪一侧行驶。GeoGuessr、Tuxun 这类地理游戏的玩家社区，已经把这项技能打磨成一门手艺，整理出成千上万条这样的定位线索。相比之下，机器地理定位系统往往只丢回一个坐标，别的什么都不说。

这种沉默，正是 GeoReasoner 想要解决的问题。这篇发表于 ICML 2024 的工作（作者来自香港科技大学（广州）、同济大学等机构）指出，街景地理定位存在两个相互纠缠的盲点。数据问题：街景数据集里混杂了大量在隧道里、对着空白墙面、或只拍到路边绿化的图像，它们都不含可用的线索。推理问题：检索式与分类式模型是黑箱，只给位置、不给任何人能检查或信任的解释。GeoReasoner 把二者视为一个整体，同时改善数据质量与可解释性。

zh.caption: 图1 街景地理定位的三种范式。检索式方法（左上）在带地理标签的图库中做相似匹配；分类式方法（左下）把地球划分为网格单元；GeoReasoner 采用的 LVLM 式方法（右）在给出位置的同时给出可读的推理理由，并按可定位性（locatability）筛选训练图像。

zh.text: 它的做法，是把大型视觉语言模型（LVLM）与从地理游戏中收集的人类推理知识配对，并且只喂给模型真正可定位的街景。回报是：在 F1 指标上，它在国家级超过最强的同类 LVLM（Qwen-VL）达 25.02%，在城市级超过 38.61%，并且在使用远少于对手的数据的情况下，略微超过专门为地理定位打造的模型，同时还能对每一步给出解释。
论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18572    代码：https://github.com/lingli1996/GeoReasoner
两个盲点：脏数据与黑箱预测
检索式方法在带地理标签的图库中找最近邻，返回其坐标，精度受限于图库是否足够完整，而完整的图库代价高昂、难以维护。分类式方法把地图切成网格并预测所属网格，忽略了招牌文字这类语义线索，同样无法说出为什么。两者还都会继承训练集中的噪声，而街景数据恰恰很脏。用没有可查内容的图像训练，模型几乎学不到什么，因此作者从清洗数据本身入手。
先量化：一张图到底能不能被定位
作者的第一步，是让可定位性（locatability）变得可度量。直觉上，当一张街景包含可供推理的东西（清晰的招牌、独特的外立面、地标）时，它就是可定位的；而当它只是隧道墙壁、或哪里都有的灌木时，就无从定位。一旦打上分数，这种反差就非常明显。

zh.caption: 图5 “可定位性”长什么样。上排为高可定位街景（loc. = 0.70 至 0.71），含招牌、独特建筑与地标；下排为低可定位街景（loc. = 0.08 至 0.19），分别是隧道、空白墙面与随处可见的植被，几乎没有可用的地理线索。

zh.text: 具体而言，可定位性是对图像语义内容的加权求和。MaskFormer 把每张街景分割成若干类别（建筑、天空、车辆、植被等），并给出每类的面积占比；Sentence-BERT 再评估每个类别与地理游戏文本线索的相关度，得到每类的权重。一张图像的可定位性，就是它的类别面积向量与这组相关度权重的点积。分数高于阈值 0.4 的图像被保留；施加该筛选后，130,000 张原始街景被筛到约 70,000 张高质量图像。
而这组相关度权重本身，来自一个 CLIP 图文配对网络，它无需任何额外的人工标注，就能学会把图像与文字对齐。

zh.caption: 图2 可定位性量化网络。以 CLIP 的方式，将街景图像与从地理游戏中挖掘的文本线索配对，得到图文相似度矩阵，再归约为每张图像的单一可定位性分数。

zh.text: 游戏中的文本线索（例如“绿底白字的路牌在韩国常用于标示高速公路信息”）由文本编码器编码，街景由图像编码器编码，两个模态之间的相似度为每张图像给出单一的可定位性分数。除了这些本就存在的游戏线索，网络不需要额外的人工标注就能完成工作。
GeoReasoner：先推理，再定位
有了干净的数据，模型以 Qwen-VL 为底座（一个视觉编码器 Vision Encoder、一个视觉语言适配器 VL Adapter、一个预训练 LLM），并用轻量的 LoRA 适配器分两阶段微调，全程保持底座权重冻结。

zh.caption: 图3 GeoReasoner 的结构与两阶段微调。模型基于 Qwen-VL（Vision Encoder、VL Adapter、预训练 LLM），先在游戏线索上学习国家级推理（Stage 1，LoRA 1），再在筛选后的街景上强化城市级预测（Stage 2，LoRA 2）；推理时同时输出 country、city 与 reasons。

zh.text: 阶段一是推理微调，在约 3,000 对来自 GeoGuessr 与 Tuxun 的图文线索上训练 LoRA 1，教会模型说出国家、并解释支持它的视觉证据。阶段二是位置微调，叠上第二个适配器 LoRA 2，在 70,000 张筛选后的街景上训练，强化细粒度的城市级预测。推理时，模型以固定的 JSON 形式作答（country、city 与一串 reasons），因此每个预测都自带依据。
结果：更少的数据，更高的精度，还有解释
在留出的街景测试集上，GeoReasoner 的国家级 F1 达到 0.9033，城市级 F1 达到 0.8585。这比 Qwen-VL 在国家级高出 25.02%，在城市级高出 38.61%。更值得注意的是，它略微超过 StreetCLIP，一个专为地理定位打造、在 1.1M 街景上训练的模型，而它自己只用了其中的 70,000 张，规模相差悬殊。

zh.caption: 表1 国家级与城市级地理定位的精确率、召回率与 F1。带 * 表示在高可定位街景上训练的模型；GeoReasoner 在两个 F1 列均领先。

zh.text: 增益从何而来？一项针对数据构成的消融，在训练预算固定的前提下，单独隔离出质量本身的作用。

zh.caption: 图7 数据质量决定精度。当训练集中高可定位图像的占比从 0% 提高到 100%，国家级（蓝）与城市级（橙）准确率都稳步上升，说明真正带来提升的是数据筛选，而非单纯的数量。

zh.text: 在其他条件不变、只改变高可定位图像比例的情况下，随着它从 0% 增加到 100%，两级准确率都稳步上升。起作用的是质量，而非数量。
抛开数字，定性表现才是这篇论文真正的重点，而它并排放在一起时最容易体会。

zh.caption: 图8 带推理的地理定位对比。在三张街景上，GeoReasoner 的判断与 LLaVA、Qwen-VL、GPT-4V 相当或更好；与黑箱基线不同，它会为每个预测给出解释（正确答案标绿，有效线索标蓝）。

zh.text: 在新加坡，ComfortDelGro 出租车直接给了 GeoReasoner 答案；在拉斯维加斯大道，它读出霓虹灯与仿制地标；在拉萨，它援引藏文与中国国旗。LLaVA 与 Qwen-VL 常常判错或凭空猜测，GPT-4V 推理不错，而 GeoReasoner 只用一小部分训练预算就与之持平。
两个阶段各自贡献了什么
第二项消融把两个微调阶段拆开来看。从 Qwen-VL 基线（国家级/城市级 F1 为 0.7225 / 0.5270）出发，只做推理微调可到 0.8215 / 0.5813，只做位置微调可到 0.8766 / 0.8255。只有两者叠加，GeoReasoner 才达到 0.9033 / 0.8585。位置微调贡献了大部分城市级精度；推理微调带来进一步提升，更关键的是带来了解释。

zh.caption: 表2 对两个微调阶段的消融。推理微调与位置微调互补，完整的两阶段模型在每个 F1 上都最优。

zh.text: 小结

GeoReasoner 的启示很简单：顶尖的地理定位模型不需要数百万张街景，而是需要对的图像与对的知识。先量化哪些街景可定位，再借用人类在地理游戏中的推理技巧，两阶段的 LVLM 就能在一小部分数据上追平甚至超越专用模型，并解释每一次判断。它也很诚实：面对真正的歧义仍会失手，比如分不清巴黎、拉斯维加斯与杭州的埃菲尔铁塔；掌握的知识也只与游戏社区写下的线索一样宽。但它给出了一条务实的路径：让地理定位既可解释，又省数据。

检索式方法在带地理标签的图库中找最近邻，返回其坐标，精度受限于图库是否足够完整，而完整的图库代价高昂、难以维护。分类式方法把地图切成网格并预测所属网格，忽略了招牌文字这类语义线索，同样无法说出为什么。两者还都会继承训练集中的噪声，而街景数据恰恰很脏。用没有可查内容的图像训练，模型几乎学不到什么，因此作者从清洗数据本身入手。

zh.title: ICML 2024 | 让视觉语言模型说清楚：这张街景到底拍在哪里
zh.subtitle: GeoReasoner 通过筛选“可定位”的街景、并借用地理游戏中的人类线索，在更少数据下超越更大的地理定位模型，还能为每次判断给出理由。

en.text: Quantifying whether an image can be located at all

The authors' first move is to make locatability measurable. Intuitively, a street view is locatable when it contains something a person could reason from, a legible sign, a distinctive facade, a landmark, and unlocatable when it is a tunnel wall or a hedge that could be anywhere. The contrast is stark once you put a number on it.

en.caption: Figure 5. What locatability looks like. Top row: highly locatable street views (loc. = 0.70 to 0.71) carry signboards, distinctive architecture, and landmarks. Bottom row: low-locatability views (loc. = 0.08 to 0.19) show a tunnel, a blank wall, and generic vegetation, with no usable geographic clue.

en.text: Concretely, locatability is a weighted sum over the semantic content of an image. MaskFormer segments each street view into classes (building, sky, vehicle, vegetation, and so on) and reports the area ratio of each. Sentence-BERT then scores how relevant each class is to the textual clues mined from geo-games, producing a weight per class. The locatability of an image is the dot product of its class-area vector with these relevance weights. Images scoring above a threshold of 0.4 are kept; applying the filter shrinks a raw pool of 130,000 street views down to roughly 70,000 high-quality ones.
The relevance weights themselves come from a CLIP image-text pairing network, which learns to align pictures with words without any extra manual labels.

en.caption: Figure 2. The locatability quantization network. A CLIP pairing of street-view images against text clues mined from geo-games yields an image-text similarity matrix, which is reduced to a single locatability score per image.

en.text: Text clues from the games (for example, green signs with white lettering indicate highways in South Korea) are embedded by a text encoder; street views are embedded by an image encoder; the similarity between the two modalities gives each image a single locatability score. Beyond the game clues that already exist, the network needs no extra manual annotation to do its job.

zh.caption: 图1 街景地理定位的三种范式。检索式方法（左上）在带地理标签的图库中做相似匹配；分类式方法（左下）把地球划分为网格单元；GeoReasoner 采用的 LVLM 式方法（右）在给出位置的同时给出可读的推理理由，并按可定位性（locatability）筛选训练图像。

zh.text: 两个阶段各自贡献了什么
第二项消融把两个微调阶段拆开来看。从 Qwen-VL 基线（国家级/城市级 F1 为 0.7225 / 0.5270）出发，只做推理微调可到 0.8215 / 0.5813，只做位置微调可到 0.8766 / 0.8255。只有两者叠加，GeoReasoner 才达到 0.9033 / 0.8585。位置微调贡献了大部分城市级精度；推理微调带来进一步提升，更关键的是带来了解释。

zh.caption: 表2 对两个微调阶段的消融。推理微调与位置微调互补，完整的两阶段模型在每个 F1 上都最优。

zh.subtitle: GeoReasoner 通过筛选“可定位”的街景、并借用地理游戏中的人类线索，在更少数据下超越更大的地理定位模型，还能为每次判断给出理由。

en.text: Show a person a random street photo and, given a few seconds, they can often name the country and sometimes the city. They do it by reading clues: the script on a shop sign, the color of a license plate, the style of a lamppost, which side of the road the cars keep to. The online communities behind games like GeoGuessr and Tuxun have turned this skill into a craft, cataloguing thousands of such tells. Machine geo-localization systems, by contrast, tend to hand back a bare coordinate and no explanation a person could follow.

That silence is the problem GeoReasoner sets out to fix. Presented at ICML 2024 by researchers from HKUST (Guangzhou), Tongji University, and collaborators, the paper argues that street-view geo-localization carries two entangled blind spots. The data problem: street-view datasets are polluted with images shot in tunnels, against blank walls, or of roadside greenery, none of which contain a usable clue. The reasoning problem: retrieval and classification models are black boxes that return a location with no explanation a human can inspect or trust. GeoReasoner treats the two as one, fixing data quality and interpretability together.

en.caption: Figure 1. Three paradigms for street-view geo-localization. Retrieval-based methods (top-left) match a query against a geo-tagged gallery; classification-based methods (bottom-left) bin the globe into cells; GeoReasoner's LVLM-based approach (right) predicts a location together with a human-readable reason, and screens training images by locatability.

en.text: Its recipe is to pair a large vision-language model (LVLM) with human inference knowledge harvested from geo-games, and to feed the model only street views that are actually locatable. The payoff is a system that beats the strongest comparable LVLM, Qwen-VL, by 25.02% at the country level and 38.61% at the city level in F1, and edges out a specialist built for geo-localization on far less data while still showing its work at every step.
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18572    Code: https://github.com/lingli1996/GeoReasoner
Two blind spots: dirty data and black-box predictions

Retrieval-based methods find the nearest neighbor in a geo-tagged gallery and return its coordinates; their accuracy is capped by how complete that gallery is, which is expensive to curate. Classification-based methods carve the map into cells and predict a cell; they ignore semantic cues such as the text on a signboard and, like retrieval, cannot say why. Both also inherit whatever noise sits in the training set, and street-view collections are noisy. A model trained on images with no findable content learns very little, so the authors start by cleaning the data itself.

zh.text: 给一个人看一张随手拍的街景照片，几秒钟内他往往能说出国家，有时还能说出城市。靠的是读线索：店招上的文字、车牌的颜色、路灯的样式、车辆靠哪一侧行驶。GeoGuessr、Tuxun 这类地理游戏的玩家社区，已经把这项技能打磨成一门手艺，整理出成千上万条这样的定位线索。相比之下，机器地理定位系统往往只丢回一个坐标，别的什么都不说。

这种沉默，正是 GeoReasoner 想要解决的问题。这篇发表于 ICML 2024 的工作（作者来自香港科技大学（广州）、同济大学等机构）指出，街景地理定位存在两个相互纠缠的盲点。数据问题：街景数据集里混杂了大量在隧道里、对着空白墙面、或只拍到路边绿化的图像，它们都不含可用的线索。推理问题：检索式与分类式模型是黑箱，只给位置、不给任何人能检查或信任的解释。GeoReasoner 把二者视为一个整体，同时改善数据质量与可解释性。

zh.caption: 图1 街景地理定位的三种范式。检索式方法（左上）在带地理标签的图库中做相似匹配；分类式方法（左下）把地球划分为网格单元；GeoReasoner 采用的 LVLM 式方法（右）在给出位置的同时给出可读的推理理由，并按可定位性（locatability）筛选训练图像。

zh.text: 它的做法，是把大型视觉语言模型（LVLM）与从地理游戏中收集的人类推理知识配对，并且只喂给模型真正可定位的街景。回报是：在 F1 指标上，它在国家级超过最强的同类 LVLM（Qwen-VL）达 25.02%，在城市级超过 38.61%，并且在使用远少于对手的数据的情况下，略微超过专门为地理定位打造的模型，同时还能对每一步给出解释。

zh.title: ICML 2024 | 让视觉语言模型说清楚：这张街景到底拍在哪里
zh.subtitle: GeoReasoner 通过筛选“可定位”的街景、并借用地理游戏中的人类线索，在更少数据下超越更大的地理定位模型，还能为每次判断给出理由。

en.caption: Figure 1. Three paradigms for street-view geo-localization. Retrieval-based methods (top-left) match a query against a geo-tagged gallery; classification-based methods (bottom-left) bin the globe into cells; GeoReasoner's LVLM-based approach (right) predicts a location together with a human-readable reason, and screens training images by locatability.

en.text: Its recipe is to pair a large vision-language model (LVLM) with human inference knowledge harvested from geo-games, and to feed the model only street views that are actually locatable. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18572    Code: https://github.com/lingli1996/GeoReasoner
Results: smaller data, higher accuracy, and an explanation

On a held-out set of street views, GeoReasoner reaches a country-level F1 of 0.9033 and a city-level F1 of 0.8585. That is 25.02% above Qwen-VL at the country level and 38.61% above it at the city level. More striking, it slightly surpasses StreetCLIP, a model built specifically for geo-localization and trained on 1.1M street views, despite using only 70,000 of them.

en.caption: Table 1. Precision, Recall, and F1 for country-level and city-level geo-localization. * marks the model trained on high-locatability street views; GeoReasoner leads both F1 columns.

en.text: Where do the gains come from? An ablation on data composition isolates the effect of quality alone, holding the training budget fixed.

en.caption: Figure 7. Data quality drives accuracy. As the share of high-locatability images in training rises from 0% to 100%, both country-level (blue) and city-level (orange) accuracy climb steadily, confirming that curation, not just volume, powers the gains.

en.text: Holding everything else fixed and varying only the fraction of high-locatability images in the training mix, accuracy rises steadily at both levels as that fraction grows from 0% to 100%. Quality, not sheer volume, is doing the work here.
Numbers aside, the qualitative behavior is really the point of the paper, and it is easiest to appreciate side by side.

en.caption: Figure 8. Geo-localization with reasoning, side by side. For three street views, GeoReasoner matches or beats LLaVA, Qwen-VL, and GPT-4V, and unlike the black-box baselines it explains each prediction (correct answers in green, useful clues in blue).

en.text: On a Singapore street the ComfortDelGro taxi gives GeoReasoner the answer; on the Las Vegas Strip it reads the neon and the replica landmarks; in Lhasa it cites Tibetan script and the Chinese flag. LLaVA and Qwen-VL often miss or guess without support, and while GPT-4V reasons well, GeoReasoner matches it on a fraction of a specialist's training budget.

zh.text: 结果：更少的数据，更高的精度，还有解释
在留出的街景测试集上，GeoReasoner 的国家级 F1 达到 0.9033，城市级 F1 达到 0.8585。这比 Qwen-VL 在国家级高出 25.02%，在城市级高出 38.61%。更值得注意的是，它略微超过 StreetCLIP，一个专为地理定位打造、在 1.1M 街景上训练的模型，而它自己只用了其中的 70,000 张，规模相差悬殊。

zh.caption: 表1 国家级与城市级地理定位的精确率、召回率与 F1。带 * 表示在高可定位街景上训练的模型；GeoReasoner 在两个 F1 列均领先。

zh.text: 增益从何而来？一项针对数据构成的消融，在训练预算固定的前提下，单独隔离出质量本身的作用。

zh.caption: 图7 数据质量决定精度。当训练集中高可定位图像的占比从 0% 提高到 100%，国家级（蓝）与城市级（橙）准确率都稳步上升，说明真正带来提升的是数据筛选，而非单纯的数量。

zh.text: 在其他条件不变、只改变高可定位图像比例的情况下，随着它从 0% 增加到 100%，两级准确率都稳步上升。起作用的是质量，而非数量。
抛开数字，定性表现才是这篇论文真正的重点，而它并排放在一起时最容易体会。

zh.caption: 图8 带推理的地理定位对比。在三张街景上，GeoReasoner 的判断与 LLaVA、Qwen-VL、GPT-4V 相当或更好；与黑箱基线不同，它会为每个预测给出解释（正确答案标绿，有效线索标蓝）。

zh.text: 在新加坡，ComfortDelGro 出租车直接给了 GeoReasoner 答案；在拉斯维加斯大道，它读出霓虹灯与仿制地标；在拉萨，它援引藏文与中国国旗。LLaVA 与 Qwen-VL 常常判错或凭空猜测，GPT-4V 推理不错，而 GeoReasoner 只用一小部分训练预算就与之持平。

zh.caption: 图8 带推理的地理定位对比。在三张街景上，GeoReasoner 的判断与 LLaVA、Qwen-VL、GPT-4V 相当或更好；与黑箱基线不同，它会为每个预测给出解释（正确答案标绿，有效线索标蓝）。

zh.text: 在新加坡，ComfortDelGro 出租车直接给了 GeoReasoner 答案；在拉斯维加斯大道，它读出霓虹灯与仿制地标；在拉萨，它援引藏文与中国国旗。LLaVA 与 Qwen-VL 常常判错或凭空猜测，GPT-4V 推理不错，而 GeoReasoner 只用一小部分训练预算就与之持平。

en.caption: Figure 1. Three paradigms for street-view geo-localization. Retrieval-based methods (top-left) match a query against a geo-tagged gallery; classification-based methods (bottom-left) bin the globe into cells; GeoReasoner's LVLM-based approach (right) predicts a location together with a human-readable reason, and screens training images by locatability.

en.text: Takeaway

GeoReasoner's headline lesson is that you do not need millions of street views to build a state-of-the-art geo-localizer; you need the right images and the right knowledge. Quantifying which views are locatable, and borrowing the inference tricks humans use to win geo-games, lets a two-stage LVLM match or beat specialist models on a fraction of the data while explaining every call. The honest boundary: the model still stumbles on genuine ambiguity, unable to tell the real Eiffel Tower in Paris from its replicas in Las Vegas and Hangzhou, and its knowledge reaches only as far as the clues the game communities have written down. zh.caption: 图1 街景地理定位的三种范式。检索式方法（左上）在带地理标签的图库中做相似匹配；分类式方法（左下）把地球划分为网格单元；GeoReasoner 采用的 LVLM 式方法（右）在给出位置的同时给出可读的推理理由，并按可定位性（locatability）筛选训练图像。

zh.text: 小结

GeoReasoner 的启示很简单：顶尖的地理定位模型不需要数百万张街景，而是需要对的图像与对的知识。先量化哪些街景可定位，再借用人类在地理游戏中的推理技巧，两阶段的 LVLM 就能在一小部分数据上追平甚至超越专用模型，并解释每一次判断。它也很诚实：面对真正的歧义仍会失手，比如分不清巴黎、拉斯维加斯与杭州的埃菲尔铁塔；掌握的知识也只与游戏社区写下的线索一样宽。但它给出了一条务实的路径：让地理定位既可解释，又省数据。
